subsystems.name: Deep-ultraviolet laser source
subsystems.role: produces the deep-ultraviolet excitation light, near 248 nanometres, that makes molecules scatter Raman light while suppressing their fluorescence.
parts: gain medium or excimer gas tube

subsystems.name: Beam delivery and collection optics
subsystems.role: focuses the laser to a small spot on the sample and collects the very weak Raman-scattered light.

subsystems.name: Spectrograph
subsystems.role: separates the returning light by wavelength so individual Raman peaks can be measured.

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: records the ultraviolet spectrum and must reject fluorescence and cosmic-ray hits.
parts: cooled charge-coupled device or CMOS sensor

subsystems.name: Sample interface and scanning
subsystems.role: positions rock, powder or other samples and keeps the laser spot in focus.
parts: surface preparation tool such as an abrasion bit

subsystems.name: Control, calibration and reference library
subsystems.role: runs the measurement, calibrates wavelengths, and matches spectra to known minerals and organic compounds.

buildSteps.title: Choose the excitation wavelength and spectral range
buildSteps.detail: Pick deep-ultraviolet excitation near 248 nanometres because it avoids most sample fluorescence and gives stronger Raman signals from organics, while still allowing a compact instrument.

buildSteps.title: Build or select the laser
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a deep-ultraviolet laser that produces stable narrow-line light at the chosen wavelength, with filters to remove unwanted colours and a shutter for safe operation.

buildSteps.title: Design the deep-ultraviolet optics
buildSteps.detail: Use reflective mirrors where possible and ultraviolet-transparent materials such as fused silica or calcium fluoride for lenses and windows. Design a dichroic to separate the strong laser light from the much weaker returning Raman light.

buildSteps.title: Build the spectrograph
buildSteps.detail: Align a slit, a diffraction grating and imaging optics in a rigid housing. Deep-ultraviolet coatings and order-sorting filters keep stray light and unwanted diffraction orders away from the detector.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the detector
buildSteps.detail: Mount a cooled ultraviolet-sensitive detector at the spectrograph focal plane, with shielding against radiation, vibration and thermal drift.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and align the instrument
buildSteps.detail: In a cleanroom, align laser, optics, spectrograph and detector. Purge or evacuate air paths where deep-ultraviolet absorption and ozone formation would weaken the beam.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and build a reference library
buildSteps.detail: Record spectra of known minerals and organic compounds, calibrate wavelength and intensity response, and store the library so the instrument can match unknown spectra automatically.

buildSteps.title: Test and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Run vibration, thermal-vacuum and radiation tests for spaceflight, or ruggedise for field use, and validate results on natural samples against established laboratory methods.

prerequisites.why: 248 nanometre light can be produced by excimer or frequency-converted solid-state lasers, though compact space-qualified versions are specialised.
fused silica and calcium fluoride transmit deep-ultraviolet light, whereas ordinary glass absorbs it.
cooled charge-coupled devices and CMOS sensors, sometimes intensified, can count the few Raman photons that return.
mineral spectra are well catalogued, but organic signatures are far more varied and mixtures remain hard to interpret.
SHERLOC on NASA's Perseverance rover has demonstrated the approach on Mars, but few such instruments have flown.

pathway.milestone: SHERLOC on the Perseverance rover maps organics and minerals in abraded Martian rock, and laboratory deep-ultraviolet Raman instruments are commercially available.
pathway.unlocks: non-destructive identification at micrometre scale without sample preparation.

pathway.milestone: Smaller, lighter deep-ultraviolet Raman systems with better fluorescence rejection and faster mapping.
pathway.unlocks: wider use on rovers, landers and portable field instruments.

pathway.milestone: Combining deep-ultraviolet Raman with other sensors such as laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy or mass spectrometry in one payload.
pathway.unlocks: more confident identification of complex organic molecules and mineral mixtures.

pathway.milestone: Stand-off or remote deep-ultraviolet Raman for outcrops and contaminated sites.
pathway.unlocks: detection without touching or preparing samples.
